literal: Firmness of mind, protecting subjects, learning, knowing, along with persevering effort—together with these five, that which is excellent is a minister.
translation: An excellent minister is one who possesses these five qualities: firmness of mind, protection of the citizens, learning, practical wisdom, and persevering effort.
modern: மனஉறுதி, குடிகளைக் காத்தல், நூல்களைக் கற்றல், அறிவுடைமை, விடாமுயற்சி ஆகிய இந்த ஐந்து பண்புகளையும் ஒருங்கே சிறப்பாகக் கொண்டிருப்பவரே அமைச்சர் ஆவார்.
explanation: This couplet defines the five essential qualities of an ideal minister. The first is 'vaṉkaṇ' (firmness of mind or courage), which is crucial for making tough decisions. The second is 'kuṭi kāttal' (protecting the citizens), ensuring the welfare of the people. The third and fourth are 'kaṟṟu' (learning) and 'ariṯal' (knowing/understanding), which represent theoretical education and its practical, wise application. The fifth is 'āḷviṉai' (persevering effort), without which no plan can succeed. A person who excels in all these five together is fit to be a minister.
